They did NOT test customer-managed private deployments (VPC-only instances), nor did they access 3rd-party reseller infra. Service-to-service traffic between Redwood services in our VPC was in scope.

High-level status with very short ETAs below; David and Rishi are looped for technical detail. 
- Finding 3 (Auth bypass via token replay): mitigation patch planned, partial fix in staging today, ETA to prod: 2026-03-08.
- Finding 4 (Sensitive fields logged in error paths): identifying services and rolling filters; ETA for complete filter rollout: 2026-03-20.
- Finding 7 (Secrets committed to S3 backup): rotation scheduled and audit of S3 lifecycle; ETA full rotation + proof: 2026-03-18.

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Technical remediation breakdown (auth + logging)

Marissa / Rishi —

Following up with technical details we can surface to BlueSky (redacted):

Finding 3 — Token replay leading to auth bypass (service-to-service path):
- Root cause: our short-lived internal JWTs lacked nonce validation on the legacy bridge service (bridge-svc).
- Short-term mitigation: added nonce validation and stricter exp checks in the token verification middleware. Deployed to staging 2026-03-06 08:30 PST.
- Long-term: rotate to signed assertion tokens with replay protection (RFC 7523 style) and add golden tests.
- ETA to prod: 2026-03-08 (rolling deploy, canary 10% --> 100%).
- Evidence to provide: staging run logs + canary rollout plan + diff (auth_patch_diff.patch).

Finding 4 — Sensitive fields in logs (error handlers across api-gateway and auth-proxy):
- Root cause: error formatting helper included "request.body" in debug logs for some 4xx handlers.
- Immediate step: updated error serializer to scrub fields named password, token, ssn, credit_card and disabled capture of full request body in production. Patch rolled to staging 2026-03-06 11:00 PST.
- Work remaining: a sweep across older microservices and middleware (approx 12 services) to apply the new serializer; also ensure log-backend (Elastic) filters are in place to redact in-flight.
- ETA: 2026-03-20 for full sweep + proof artifacts (grep results + Confluence pages).

I'll push the PR links privately; Rishi to coordinate the secrets rotation plan.

-David
David Kim
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: auth_patch_diff.patch

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 7 Mar 2026 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Secrets rotation & permissions changes

Marissa / David —

Secrets finding (S3 backup snapshot with embedded config): status update and plan:
- What happened: nightly backup job included a debug snapshot of a service container; one snapshot inadvertently contained an env file with a deploy key. The snapshot is in a private S3 bucket with restrictive IAM, not public.
- Immediate actions taken (already done):
  - Revoked the discovered deploy key 2026-03-05 22:10 PST.
  - Created new KMS-wrapped keys and started rotation for affected services.
  - Removed the offending snapshot and triggered S3 object deletion lifecycle; requested TrustGuard confirm they were not able to access the object.
- Next steps & ETAs:
  - Full rotation of all keys referenced in the snapshot: ETA 2026-03-18 (scripts and runbook ready).
  - Permission hardening: tighten IAM policies on backup role + add object-level scanning pre-upload: ETA 2026-03-12.
  - Evidence items: KMS rotation logs, new key fingerprints, S3 object deletion records.

I'll attach the rotation runbook to the tracker and link PRs. If BlueSky needs PKI-level evidence, we can produce KMS audit entries and CloudTrail ranges.

-Rishi
Staff Software Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference

Hi Elena,

Appended below is a concise remediation status for Findings 3, 4, and 7 plus the evidence we can provide. Full redacted report and the tracker are attached. If you prefer a shared folder with limited access, say the word and we'll grant it.

Summary (most important items):
- Finding 3 (Auth replay) — STATUS: Fixed in prod 2026-03-08. Evidence: canary rollout logs, auth_patch_diff.patch, token validation tests.
- Finding 4 (Sensitive logging) — STATUS: In progress. Action: new error serializer pushed to staging; sweep across 12 services in progress. ETA: 2026-03-20. Evidence planned: grep outputs showing scrubbing, Confluence page, CloudWatch/Elastic index filters.
- Finding 7 (Secrets in S3 backup) — STATUS: Mitigated and rotating. Actions completed: key revoked, offending snapshot removed. Remaining: full rotation of referenced keys and IAM hardening. ETA for complete rotation + proof: 2026-03-18. Evidence planned: KMS rotation logs, CloudTrail deletion records.

Owners and primary contacts: David Kim (auth, logging) and Rishi Malhotra (secrets, permissions). Evelyn Hart (Legal) is cc'd for any compliance language or redaction sign-off.

Next steps:

Thanks,
